title: Voltage, Current, Resistance, and Power
summary: Use safe mathematical scenarios to connect electrical quantities.
objectives: Use P = V x I in synthetic problems.
Describe voltage, current, resistance, power, and energy conceptually.

vocab.def: Electrical potential difference in a circuit model.
The rate of charge flow in a circuit model.
A property that opposes current in a circuit model.
The rate at which energy is transferred or used.

sections.heading: Calculate safely
sections.body: In a synthetic scenario, 120 volts and 5 amps represent P = V x I = 600 watts. This is mathematical practice, not permission to measure a live system.

sections.heading: Ohm's Law depth
sections.body: Grade 11 includes V = I x R through diagrams and calculations only. Live mains measurement is excluded.

practice.prompt: A model load is 24 V and 2 A. What power does it represent?

quiz.question: What does P = V x I calculate in a simple model?

lab.objective: Calculate synthetic power values without live measurement.

reflectionPrompt: What assumption did your calculation require?
